title: Identifying ICAM-1 as a Therapeutic Target for Cytokine Storm in Human Macrophages Through Integrative Bioinformatics Approaches.
authors: Chen, Shaojun; Wu, Dapeng; Zheng, Zhe; Luo, Yiyuan; Zhang, Lihua
one_liner_zh: 该文通过生物信息学分析鉴定细胞因子风暴关键基因ICAM-1，并用分子对接/MD模拟研究药物达沙替尼与ICAM-1蛋白的相互作用，但核心是蛋白-小分子药物互作而非蛋白质-DNA互作，且无TF-DNA结合建模，仅方法上MD可借鉴，与课题关联较弱。
abstract: Excessive macrophage activation is thought to be the primary cause of the cytokine storm that results in severe coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) complications. The underlying mechanisms remain elusive, and more research is needed to find disease-critical genes and develop effective therapies. In this study, we used publicly accessible microarray datasets of cytokine storm in cultured human monocyte-derived macrophages challenged with cytokines, and employed bioinformatics, such as weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) and differential expression analysis, to dissect gene expression profiles and identify putative disease-related molecules. Initially, three co-expression modules and related key genes were discovered, which highly correlated to macrophages challenged with cytokines. Then, a preliminary gene expression signature consisting of 203 upregulated and 24 downregulated genes was identified. Next, protein-protein interaction analysis and hub gene identification were used to identify 11 crucial hub genes, namely tripartite motif-containing 21 (TRIM21), interferon regulatory factor 1 (IRF1), guanylate binding protein 1 (GBP1), transporter associated with antigen processing 1 (TAP1), nuclear myosin I (NMI), interleukin 15 receptor subunit alpha (IL15RA), apolipoprotein L1 (APOL1), intercellular adhesion molecule 1 (ICAM-1), protein tyrosine phosphatase non-receptor type 1 (PTPN1), E74-like ETS transcription factor 4 (ELF4) and guanylate binding protein 2 (GBP2). Then, the LINCS L1000 characteristic direction signatures search engine (L1000CDS2) was employed for drug repurposing studies. Dasatinib was predicted to be the leading therapeutic compound to perturb the gene signature of cytokine storm in human macrophages. Connectivity Map results suggested that dasatinib may normalize ICAM-1 expression. In addition, the results of molecular docking studies and molecular dynamics simulation revealed that dasatinib may spontaneously interact with ICAM-1 via several key residues and form a relatively stable protein-ligand complex. Overall, this work, based on an analysis of co-expression correlation networks, gene expression signatures and pivotal genes in human macrophages challenged with cytokines, combined with drug repurposing studies, demonstrated that dasatinib may interact with ICAM-1 and could be a potential candidate for cytokine storm. However, due to the limitations of computational approaches, further experimental validation is necessary.
abstract_zh: 巨噬细胞过度活化被认为是导致严重冠状病毒病2019（COVID-19）并发症中细胞因子风暴的主要原因。其潜在机制仍不清楚，需要更多研究来发现疾病关键基因并开发有效疗法。在本研究中，我们使用了公开可获取的微阵列数据集，这些数据集涉及培养的人单核细胞来源巨噬细胞在细胞因子刺激下的细胞因子风暴，并采用生物信息学方法，如加权基因共表达网络分析（WGCNA）和差异表达分析，来解析基因表达谱并识别可能的疾病相关分子。首先，发现了三个与细胞因子刺激的巨噬细胞高度相关的共表达模块及相关关键基因。随后，鉴定出一个初步的基因表达特征，包括203个上调基因和24个下调基因。接下来，通过蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用分析和枢纽基因识别，确定了11个关键枢纽基因，即三基序包含蛋白21（TRIM21）、干扰素调节因子1（IRF1）、鸟苷酸结合蛋白1（GBP1）、抗原加工相关转运体1（TAP1）、核肌球蛋白I（NMI）、白细胞介素15受体亚基α（IL15RA）、载脂蛋白L1（APOL1）、细胞间黏附分子1（ICAM-1）、蛋白酪氨酸磷酸酶非受体型1（PTPN1）、E74样ETS转录因子4（ELF4）和鸟苷酸结合蛋白2（GBP2）。然后，使用LINCS L1000特征方向签名搜索引擎（L1000CDS2）进行药物重定位研究。预测达沙替尼（Dasatinib）是扰动人类巨噬细胞中细胞因子风暴基因特征的主要治疗化合物。Connectivity Map结果表明，达沙替尼可能使ICAM-1表达正常化。此外，分子对接研究和分子动力学模拟结果显示，达沙替尼可能通过几个关键残基与ICAM-1自发相互作用，并形成相对稳定的蛋白质-配体复合物。总体而言，本研究基于对细胞因子刺激的人类巨噬细胞中共表达相关网络、基因表达特征和关键基因的分析，结合药物重定位研究，表明达沙替尼可能与ICAM-1相互作用，并可能成为细胞因子风暴的潜在候选药物。然而，由于计算方法的局限性，进一步的实验验证是必要的。
